newsitem.title: INDONESIA: World coffee producers, users to review market.
newsitem.headline: World coffee producers, users to review market.

text.p: The world's leading coffee producers and consumers met on Monday on the Indonesian island of Bali to discuss the instability in the market over the past six months and find ways to stabilise volatile prices.

The three-day meeting of the 61-member International Coffee Organization (ICO) was to be followed by a gathering of coffee producers from the Asia-Pacific region and a meeting of robusta producers on Thursday.
"It has been a difficult time because there's been a little bit of instability in the market," ICO executive director Celsius Lodder told Reuters.

"Prices last year have been quite volatile. The fundamentals of demand, supply and stocks, weather conditions...elements you use to analyse the market, they are not explaining price movement," he said.
He said that judging from the fundamentals of the demand side, prices would be expected to be much higher and to induce players to look at the market more favourably in terms of price.
"So what's happening here? To give an answer to that, we are proposing to hold a seminar in May on price determination. Why the fundamentals are not explaining price variations 100 percent.
"They still explain a lot of things...but not 100 percent. You have other factors. The just-in-time policy of roasters, technical analyses on futures...we like to talk about that."
Lodder said last October that world coffee output would be between 99 million and 100 million 60-kg bags in the 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) coffee year.

He said demand was expected to be about 98 million bags, including about 25 million bags consumed in producing countries. He said demand by consumer countries would total between 72 million and 73 million bags in the same coffee year.
Members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) decided at a meeting in Brazil on January 23 to further cut exports by 1.3 million bags in the first half of this year.
A previous plan by the 14-member grouping to cut consumer stocks and bolster prices had decided to limit their exports to 26.28 million bags between January and June this year.

The 1.3 million-bag reduction would be divided into one million bags for robusta producers and 300,000 bags for arabica producers. Robusta producers are expected to decide on the allocation at their Bali meeting on Thursday.
The move to reduce robusta exports was initiated by the InterAfrican Coffee Organisation in a bid to lift prices.
Industry sources said Indonesia, the world's top robusta producer, had offered to cut its exports by 150,000 bags, leaving the bulk of the reduction to be carried by African producers.
"We told the meeting in Brazil that we can only afford to reduce exports by 150,000 bags," one Indonesian source said. "We are going to leave it to them to sort the rest out."
The sources said Ivory Coast Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Emmanuel Gauze was expected to chair the meeting of robusta producers.
"He (Gauze) has to take the initiative to get all the robusta producers together at the meeting," one source said. "We'll have to wait and see if he can get the allocations sorted out."

Indonesia has been cool to the proposal because its regional trade rival, Vietnam is not an ACPC member and therefore is not obliged to participate in the programme. Vietnam will not be attending the robusta group meeting.
